name: Access Point

steps.text: Plug the first Access Point into an unswitched wall outlet.
Tap the SET button four times rapidly to start phase detection (setup) mode.
steps.expect: Continuous beep, once per second; LED turns on bright green

steps.text: Plug the second Access Point into an unswitched outlet, preferably on the other side of the home.

Watch the LED on the second Access Point. If it blinks green, the two are on opposite phases; if it blinks red and green or is solid red or green, they are on the same phase, so unplug the second Access Point and try another outlet.
steps.expect: Second Access Point LED blinks green

steps.text: Tap the SET button on the first Access Point to leave setup mode.
steps.expect: First Access Point stops beeping; both LEDs turn dim green

notes: The first Access Point stays in setup mode for about 9 minutes; if it times out, start setup mode again.
Install at least two Access Points or other dual-band devices before setting up other Insteon devices; add one for every 750 to 1,000 square feet in larger homes.
Don't use an outlet controlled by a switch, a filtered power strip, an AC line filter, a UPS or another module's pass-through outlet, and keep it away from large metal objects.
To add more Access Points, put the first one in setup mode and check each new one the same way.
With one Access Point only, check RF coverage by tapping an RF-only device's SET button (or holding a scene button) where it will be used and watching the Access Point's LED.
Access Points below revision 2.0 have a white LED instead of the red and green LED; the Access Point 2443 Owner's Manual has a table of how mixed revisions behave.
Insteon later reused the model number 2443 for the Micro On/Off Module, whose identities are its own.
